name: BeO bromellite (crystal no. 1 in air)
citation: R. M. Hazen and L. W. Finger (1986). High-pressure and high-temperature crystal chemistry of beryllium oxide. Journal of Applied Physics 59, 3728–3733. DOI: 10.1063/1.336756.
conditions_evidence: Original CIF identifies crystal no. 1 in air. It supplies no numeric temperature or pressure for this record. The study includes pressure and temperature series, but those other conditions are not assigned to this in-air entry.
method: Experimental single-crystal diffraction structure of synthetic bromellite from the authors' pressure/temperature study.
synthesis_conditions_note: Original CIF says Synthetic; numeric synthesis conditions not established here.
selection: Experimental ordered in-air BeO structure; both inequivalent element sites and each complete split four-neighbor shell retained. No ideal-wurtzite coordinate substitution.
notes: The raw coordinates 0.33333/0.66667 are rounded to exact crystallographic thirds by the parser; source bytes are unchanged. The measured oxygen z=0.37810 is retained.

Each selected Be or O site has multiplicity 2 and population weight 1 within its own absorber species. Each first shell contains 3 neighbors at 1.646724428 Å and 1 at 1.655170560 Å; these distances must not be collapsed into an average.

Low-energy light-element K-edge FEFF paths are unvalidated candidate scattering references, not a demonstration of usable measured EXAFS or XANES accuracy. Core excitons, band structure, charge transfer and nonspherical potentials can matter near these edges; retain actual SCF convergence, potential and executable diagnostics.

A nominal native k grid is not an experimental usable k range. Choose an absorber/edge-appropriate measured range and validate against data; a converged FEFF calculation alone does not validate this reference.
